To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the prediction accuracy is a function of amino acid type and its secondary structure class and also the accuracy of prediction is a function of secondary structure class.

1) the expertness of secondary structure prediction is not a constant and it depends on the type of the amino acid and the type of secondary structure class, 2) the accuracy of secondary structure prediction in beta strand is less than other classes, 3) Proline and Glycin amino acids are the worst predicted amino acids, 4) the prediction of alpha helices is more accurate than beta strands and 5) the prediction accuracy of beta sheets and beta turns are similar.
there is a harmony between prediction behavior of amino acids in all engines and the prediction accuracy of each amino acid type in each secondary structure is proportional to its global propensity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expertness of secondary structure prediction and it has been shown that the accuracy of secondary structure prediction is dependent to the amino acid prediction accuracy.
the expertness assessment of the secondary structure prediction engines and the new criterion could be used as a useful tool for the future development of the prediction methods.
the expertness assessment of protein secondary structure engines and a new criterion is introduced to improve the accuracy of prediction engines in this field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the accuracy of prediction is not only related to amino acid index, but it is also related to the amino acid type and its secondary structure type.
the prediction of beta strands is more difficult than the other secondary structures and the accuracy of prediction is directly proportional to its expertness.
, the prediction accuracy is not only related to amino acid type, but also to the secondary structure class in which it is located.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expertness of a prediction engine could not be evaluated only based on the overall prediction accuracy.
the expertness of secondary structure prediction is an important issue that should be studied in more details.

the expertness of prediction engines could be improved if the prediction accuracy of Proline and Glycin in alpha helix and beta strand classes and also the prediction accuracy of beta strands in each engine could be increased.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accuracy of prediction of secondary structure is highly dependent on amino acid index and its prediction accuracy is not independent of amino acid type.
a new expertness index has been introduced and used for reevaluation of the prediction accuracy of some protein secondary structure prediction servers.
the accuracy of the secondary structure prediction engines is highly correlated with the accuracy of prediction of amino acid types and their global propensities.
